$comment: Shared table for hdf-to-sarif's URI rendering, read by go/uri_test.go and typescript/uri.test.ts so neither language can drift. SARIF puts format 'uri-reference' on artifactLocation.uri and format 'uri' on helpUri/informationUri, and real scanner output does not respect either. 'reference' is what EncodeURIReference/encodeUriReference must return; 'absolute' is what AbsoluteURI/absoluteUri must return, with "" meaning the value is dropped because it has no scheme.

cases.why: an ordinary relative source path is already a valid uri-reference, and is not an absolute URI
a real ZAP URL that needs no encoding at all
the defect: a real ZAP ref carrying a template placeholder, which no URI grammar accepts. The encoded form is the one ZAP itself emits for the same construct elsewhere in the same scan
an already-encoded triplet is left alone rather than double-encoded, so encoding is idempotent on its own output
a real ZAP SQL-injection probe: + and - and ? and = are all sub-delims or gen-delims and stay as themselves
a Windows path: backslash and space are not in any RFC 3986 set. The drive letter makes it parse as a scheme, which is a known URI ambiguity and not this function's to resolve
spaces are encoded; no scheme, so the absolute form is dropped
a bare percent is not a pct-encoded triplet and is itself encoded, so the output is always decodable
a truncated triplet is not a triplet
a percent followed by non-hex is not a triplet
a non-ASCII byte is encoded per UTF-8 byte, which is why both languages encode bytes and not code units
the empty string is a legal uri-reference and is not an absolute URI
free text in a helpUri field is dropped rather than emitted into a field with format uri
a relative reference is valid for artifactLocation.uri but not for helpUri
a non-http scheme is still an absolute URI

a scheme must start with a letter, so this is a relative reference whose first segment merely looks like one — and RFC 3986 §4.2 forbids a colon in a relative reference's first segment, so the colon is encoded. Measured, not assumed: the unencoded form is rejected by the uri-reference format
